sanskrit: nigṛhya tu rathānīkaṃ kaṅkapatraiḥ śilāśitaiḥ āsasāda raṇe pārthaḥ suśarmāṇaṃ mahāratham
english: Having checked the array of chariots with heron-feathered shafts whetted on stone, Pārtha closed in battle upon Suśarman, that mighty car-warrior.

sanskrit: sa tasya śaravarṣāṇi vavarṣa rathināṃ varaḥ tathā saṃśaptakāś caiva pārthasya samare sthitāḥ
english: That best of car-warriors rained down showers of arrows upon him, and the saṃśaptakas too, standing firm in the fight, poured them upon Pārtha.

sanskrit: suśarmā tu tataḥ pārthaṃ viddhvā navabhir āśugaiḥ janārdanaṃ tribhir bāṇair abhyahan dakṣiṇe bhuje tato 'pareṇa bhallena ketuṃ vivyādha māriṣa
english: Then Suśarman, having pierced Pārtha with nine swift arrows, struck Janārdana on the right arm with three shafts, and with yet another broad-headed arrow he pierced the banner, O honoured one.

sanskrit: sa vānaravaro rājan viśvakarmakṛto mahān nanāda sumahan nādaṃ bhīṣayan vai nanarda ca
english: That great monkey upon the banner, O king, the work of Viśvakarman, gave a mighty roar and roared again, striking terror all around.

sanskrit: kapes tu ninadaṃ śrutvā saṃtrastā tava vāhinī bhayaṃ vipulam ādāya niśceṣṭā samapadyata
english: Hearing the cry of the monkey, your army, struck with terror and seized by overwhelming fear, became wholly motionless.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā śuśubhe senā niśceṣṭāvasthitā nṛpa nānāpuṣpasamākīrṇaṃ yathā caitrarathaṃ vanam
english: Then that host, standing motionless, gleamed, O king, like the grove of Caitraratha strewn with blossoms of every kind.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ yodhās te kurusattama arjunaṃ siṣicur bāṇaiḥ parvataṃ jaladā iva parivavrus tadā sarve pāṇḍavasya mahāratham
english: Then recovering their senses, O best of the Kurus, those warriors drenched Arjuna with arrows as rain-clouds drench a mountain, and they all encircled the great car of the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: te hayān rathacakre ca ratheṣāś cāpi bhārata nigṛhya balavat tūrṇaṃ siṃhanādam athānadan
english: Seizing forcibly and at once the horses, the chariot-wheels, and the chariot-shafts, O Bhārata, they then let loose a lion's roar.

sanskrit: apare jagṛhuś caiva keśavasya mahābhujau pārtham anye mahārāja rathasthaṃ jagṛhur mudā
english: Others seized the mighty arms of Keśava, while still others, O great king, joyfully laid hold of Pārtha as he stood upon his car.

sanskrit: keśavas tu tadā bāhū vidhunvan raṇamūrdhani pātayām āsa tān sarvān duṣṭahastīva hastinaḥ
english: But Keśava, shaking his arms there at the head of the battle, flung them all down as a rogue elephant flings other elephants.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho raṇe pārthaḥ saṃvṛtas tair mahārathaiḥ nigṛhītaṃ rathaṃ dṛṣṭvā keśavaṃ cāpy abhidrutam rathārūḍhāṃś ca subahūn padātīṃś cāpy apātayat
english: Then Pārtha, enraged in battle, hemmed in by those great car-warriors, seeing his chariot held fast and Keśava set upon, struck down very many who rode in chariots and many footmen besides.

sanskrit: āsannāṃś ca tato yodhāñ śarair āsannayodhibhiḥ cyāvayām āsa samare keśavaṃ cedam abravīt
english: And then with close-fighting arrows he made the warriors who pressed close fall away in the fight, and he spoke thus to Keśava.

sanskrit: paśya kṛṣṇa mahābāho saṃśaptakagaṇān mayā kurvāṇān dāruṇaṃ karma vadhyamānān sahasraśaḥ
english: Behold, mighty-armed Kṛṣṇa, the bands of saṃśaptakas, who wrought a dreadful deed, now slain by me in their thousands.

sanskrit: rathabandham imaṃ ghoraṃ pṛthivyāṃ nāsti kaś cana yaḥ saheta pumāṃl loke mad anyo yadupuṃgava
english: There is no man upon earth, O bull of the Yadus, none in the world save myself, who could endure this dread blockade of the chariot.

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā bībhatsur devadattam athādhamat pāñcajanyaṃ ca kṛṣṇo 'pi pūrayann iva rodasī
english: Having spoken thus, Bībhatsu blew his Devadatta, and Kṛṣṇa too blew the Pāñcajanya, as though filling heaven and earth with sound.

sanskrit: taṃ tu śaṅkhasvanaṃ śrutvā saṃśaptakavarūthinī saṃcacāla mahārāja vitrastā cābhavad bhṛśam
english: Hearing that blast of the conches, the host of the saṃśaptakas reeled, O great king, and was sorely terrified.

sanskrit: padabandhaṃ tataś cakre pāṇḍavaḥ paravīrahā nāgam astraṃ mahārāja saṃprodīrya muhur muhuḥ
english: Then the Pāṇḍava, slayer of hostile heroes, wrought a foot-binding snare, O great king, invoking again and again the serpent-weapon.

sanskrit: yān uddiśya raṇe pārthaḥ padabandhaṃ cakāra ha te baddhāḥ padabandhena pāṇḍavena mahātmanā niśceṣṭā abhavan rājann aśmasāramayā iva
english: Those against whom Pārtha wrought the foot-binding snare in battle, bound by the foot-snare of the great-souled Pāṇḍava, became motionless, O king, as though made of iron.

sanskrit: niśceṣṭāṃs tu tato yodhān avadhīt pāṇḍunandanaḥ yathendraḥ samare daityāṃs tārakasya vadhe purā
english: Then the son of Pāṇḍu slew those motionless warriors, as Indra of old slew the Daityas in the battle at the killing of Tāraka.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare mumucus taṃ rathottamam āyudhāni ca sarvāṇi visraṣṭum upacakramuḥ
english: Being slaughtered in the fight, they let go that splendid chariot and began to cast away all their weapons.

sanskrit: tataḥ suśarmā rājendra gṛhītāṃ vīkṣya vāhinīm sauparṇam astraṃ tvaritaḥ prāduścakre mahārathaḥ
english: Then Suśarman, O lord of kings, seeing his host held captive, swiftly brought forth the Garuḍa-weapon, that great car-warrior.

sanskrit: tataḥ suparṇāḥ saṃpetur bhakṣayanto bhujaṃgamān te vai vidudruvur nāgā dṛṣṭvā tān khacarān nṛpa
english: Thereupon eagles swooped down, devouring the serpents, and those serpents fled away, O king, at the sight of the sky-rangers.

sanskrit: babhau balaṃ tad vimuktaṃ padabandhād viśāṃ pate meghavṛndād yathā mukto bhāskaras tāpayan prajāḥ
english: That host, freed from the foot-binding snare, shone forth, O lord of peoples, like the sun released from a mass of clouds, scorching the creatures.

sanskrit: vipramuktās tu te yodhāḥ phalgunasya rathaṃ prati sasṛjur bāṇasaṃghāṃś ca śastrasaṃghāṃś ca māriṣa
english: Those warriors, set free, hurled volleys of arrows and volleys of weapons against the chariot of Phalguna, O honoured one.

sanskrit: tāṃ mahāstramayīṃ vṛṣṭiṃ saṃchidya śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ vyavātiṣṭhat tato yodhān vāsaviḥ paravīrahā
english: Cutting apart that downpour wrought of mighty weapons with showers of his own arrows, the son of Vāsava, slayer of hostile heroes, then held the warriors at bay.

sanskrit: suśarmā tu tato rājan bāṇenānataparvaṇā arjunaṃ hṛdaye viddhvā vivyādhānyais tribhiḥ śaraiḥ sa gāḍhaviddho vyathito rathopastha upāviśat
english: Then Suśarman, O king, having pierced Arjuna in the heart with a smooth-jointed arrow, struck him again with three more shafts; deeply wounded and pained, Arjuna sank down upon the floor of his chariot.

sanskrit: pratilabhya tataḥ saṃjñāṃ śvetāśvaḥ kṛṣṇasārathiḥ aindram astram ameyātmā prāduścakre tvarānvitaḥ tato bāṇasahasrāṇi samutpannāni māriṣa
english: Then recovering his senses, he of the white horses and Kṛṣṇa for charioteer, that immeasurable one, swiftly brought forth the Aindra weapon; and thereupon thousands of arrows came into being, O honoured one.

sanskrit: sarvadikṣu vyadṛśyanta sūdayanto nṛpa dvipān hayān rathāṃś ca samare śastraiḥ śatasahasraśaḥ
english: In every quarter they were seen, destroying in battle elephants, horses, and chariots with their weapons by the hundreds of thousands, O king.

sanskrit: vadhyamāne tataḥ sainye vipulā bhīḥ samāviśat saṃśaptakagaṇānāṃ ca gopālānāṃ ca bhārata na hi kaś cit pumāṃs tatra yo 'rjunaṃ pratyayudhyata
english: As the host was being slaughtered, a vast terror entered the bands of the saṃśaptakas and the cowherds, O Bhārata; for there was no man there who could fight back against Arjuna.

sanskrit: paśyatāṃ tatra vīrāṇām ahanyata mahad balam hanyamānam apaśyaṃś ca niśceṣṭāḥ sma parākrame
english: Before the very eyes of those heroes the great army was slain, and watching it being cut down, they stood helpless to exert their valour.

sanskrit: ayutaṃ tatra yodhānāṃ hatvā pāṇḍusuto raṇe vyabhrājata raṇe rājan vidhūmo 'gnir iva jvalan
english: Having slain ten thousand warriors there in the fight, the son of Pāṇḍu blazed forth in battle, O king, like a smokeless fire flaming high.

sanskrit: caturdaśa sahasrāṇi yāni śiṣṭāni bhārata rathānām ayutaṃ caiva trisāhasrāś ca dantinaḥ
english: Of those that remained, O Bhārata, there were fourteen thousand foot, ten thousand chariots, and three thousand tuskers.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃśaptakā bhūyaḥ parivavrur dhanaṃjayam martavyam iti niścitya jayaṃ vāpi nivartanam
english: Then the saṃśaptakas once more encircled Dhanaṃjaya, having resolved either to die or to win victory and turn him back.

sanskrit: tatra yuddhaṃ mahad dhy āsīt tāvakānāṃ viśāṃ pate śūreṇa balinā sārdhaṃ pāṇḍavena kirīṭinā
english: And there a great battle was joined, O lord of peoples, between your men and the valiant, mighty Pāṇḍava, the diademed one.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca kṛtavarmā kṛpo drauṇiḥ sūtaputraś ca māriṣa ulūkaḥ saubalaś caiva rājā ca saha sodaraiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Kṛtavarman, Kṛpa, Droṇa's son, and the Sūta's son, O honoured one, Ulūka and the son of Subala, and the king together with his brothers—

sanskrit: sīdamānāṃ camūṃ dṛṣṭvā pāṇḍuputrabhayārditām samujjihīrṣur vegena bhinnāṃ nāvam ivārṇave
english: seeing their army sinking, tormented by fear of the son of Pāṇḍu, sought eagerly to lift it up, as one would a foundering ship upon the sea.

sanskrit: tato yuddham atīvāsīn muhūrtam iva bhārata bhīrūṇāṃ trāsajananaṃ śūrāṇāṃ harṣavardhanam
english: Then for a moment, as it were, there was a most fierce battle, O Bhārata, breeding terror in the timid and swelling the joy of the brave.

sanskrit: kṛpeṇa śaravarṣāṇi vipramuktāni saṃyuge sṛñjayāḥ śātayām āsuḥ śalabhānāṃ vrajā iva
english: The showers of arrows let loose by Kṛpa in the encounter the Sṛñjayas cut to pieces, like swarms of locusts.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī tu tataḥ kruddho gautamaṃ tvarito yayau vavarṣa śaravarṣāṇi samantād eva brāhmaṇe
english: Then Śikhaṇḍin, enraged, rushed swiftly upon the son of Gautama and rained showers of arrows on every side upon the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: kṛpas tu śaravarṣaṃ tad vinihatya mahāstravit śikhaṇḍinaṃ raṇe kruddho vivyādha daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: But Kṛpa, knower of mighty weapons, having beaten back that shower of arrows, in his wrath pierced Śikhaṇḍin in the fight with ten shafts.

sanskrit: tataḥ śikhaṇḍī kupītaḥ śaraiḥ saptabhir āhave kṛpaṃ vivyādha subhṛśaṃ kaṅkapatrair ajihmagaiḥ
english: Then Śikhaṇḍin, incensed, pierced Kṛpa most sorely in the battle with seven straight-flying, heron-feathered arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛpaḥ śarais tīkṣṇaiḥ so 'tividdho mahārathaḥ vyaśvasūtarathaṃ cakre pārṣataṃ tu dvijottamaḥ
english: Then Kṛpa, that great car-warrior, sorely pierced by sharp arrows, best of the twice-born, deprived the son of Pṛṣata of horses, charioteer, and car.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt tu tato yānād avaplutya mahārathaḥ carmakhaḍge ca saṃgṛhya satvaraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ yayau
english: Then that great car-warrior, leaping down from the car whose horses were slain, seized shield and sword and rushed swiftly upon the Brāhmaṇa.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ chādayām āsa samare tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: As he came rushing on, Kṛpa covered him at once in the fight with smooth-jointed arrows, and that seemed a wondrous thing.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma śilānāṃ plavanaṃ yathā niśceṣṭo yad raṇe rājañ śikhaṇḍī samatiṣṭhata
english: There we beheld a marvel like stones floating upon water, that Śikhaṇḍin stood motionless in the fight, O king.

sanskrit: kṛpeṇa chāditaṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpottama śikhaṇḍinam pratyudyayau kṛpaṃ tūrṇaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumno mahārathaḥ
english: Seeing Śikhaṇḍin overwhelmed by Kṛpa, O best of kings, the great car-warrior Dhṛṣṭadyumna at once advanced against Kṛpa.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ tato yāntaṃ śāradvatarathaṃ prati pratijagrāha vegena kṛtavarmā mahārathaḥ
english: As Dhṛṣṭadyumna then advanced against the chariot of Śāradvata's son, the great car-warrior Kṛtavarman impetuously took him in hand.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiram athāyāntaṃ śāradvatarathaṃ prati saputraṃ sahasenaṃ ca droṇaputro nyavārayat
english: And as Yudhiṣṭhira advanced against the chariot of Śāradvata's son, together with his sons and with his army, Droṇa's son held him off.

sanskrit: nakulaṃ sahadevaṃ ca tvaramāṇau mahārathau pratijagrāha te putraḥ śaravarṣeṇa vārayan
english: Nakula and Sahadeva, those two great car-warriors pressing forward, your son met and held back with a shower of arrows.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ karūṣāṃś ca kekayān sahasṛñjayān karṇo vaikartano yuddhe vārayām āsa bhārata
english: Bhīmasena, the Karūṣas, the Kekayas together with the Sṛñjayas—these Karṇa, son of Vikartana, held off in the battle, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍinas tato bāṇān kṛpaḥ śāradvato yudhi prāhiṇot tvarayā yukto didhakṣur iva māriṣa
english: Then Kṛpa, son of Śaradvat, hastened to send arrows against Śikhaṇḍin in the fight, as though eager to consume him, O honoured one.

sanskrit: tāñ śarān preṣitāṃs tena samantād dhemabhūṣaṇān ciccheda khaḍgam āvidhya bhrāmayaṃś ca punaḥ punaḥ
english: Those gold-adorned arrows sent by him on every side Śikhaṇḍin cut apart, swinging and whirling his sword again and again.

sanskrit: śatacandraṃ tataś carma gautamaḥ pārṣatasya ha vyadhamat sāyakais tūrṇaṃ tata uccukruśur janāḥ
english: Then the son of Gautama swiftly shattered with his shafts the hundred-mooned shield of Pṛṣata's son, and thereupon the people raised a great cry.

sanskrit: sa vicarmā mahārāja khaḍgapāṇir upādravat kṛpasya vaśam āpanno mṛtyor āsyam ivāturaḥ
english: Bereft of his shield, O great king, sword in hand, he rushed on, fallen into Kṛpa's power like a stricken man into the jaws of death.

sanskrit: śāradvataśarair grastaṃ kliśyamānaṃ mahābalam citraketusuto rājan suketus tvarito yayau
english: Seeing that mighty warrior engulfed and harassed by the arrows of Śaradvat's son, Suketu, the son of Citraketu, O king, hastened forth.

sanskrit: vikiran brāhmaṇaṃ yuddhe bahubhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ abhyāpatad ameyātmā gautamasya rathaṃ prati
english: Scattering many sharp arrows upon the Brāhmaṇa in the fight, that one of immeasurable spirit charged against the chariot of Gautama's son.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvāviṣahyaṃ taṃ yuddhe brāhmaṇaṃ caritavratam apayātas tatas tūrṇaṃ śikhaṇḍī rājasattama
english: Seeing that Brāhmaṇa of steadfast vows irresistible in the fight, Śikhaṇḍin then swiftly withdrew, O best of kings.

sanskrit: suketus tu tato rājan gautamaṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ viddhvā vivyādha saptatyā punaś cainaṃ tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Suketu, O king, having pierced the son of Gautama with nine arrows, struck him with seventy more, and again with three shafts.

sanskrit: athāsya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ punaś ciccheda māriṣa sārathiṃ ca śareṇāsya bhṛśaṃ marmaṇy atāḍayat
english: Then he cut apart his bow together with the arrow set to it, O honoured one, and struck his charioteer sorely in a vital spot with a shaft.

sanskrit: gautamas tu tataḥ kruddho dhanur gṛhya navaṃ dṛḍham suketuṃ triṃśatā bāṇaiḥ sarvamarmasv atāḍayat
english: But the son of Gautama, then enraged, taking up a new and firm bow, struck Suketu with thirty arrows in all his vital points.

sanskrit: sa vihvalitasarvāṅgaḥ pracacāla rathottame bhūmicāle yathā vṛkṣaś calaty ākampito bhṛśam
english: With all his limbs unstrung, he reeled upon his splendid chariot, as a tree sways, violently shaken, in an earthquake.

sanskrit: calatas tasya kāyāt tu śiro jvalitakuṇḍalam soṣṇīṣaṃ saśirastrāṇaṃ kṣurapreṇānvapātayat
english: From his swaying body Kṛpa, with a razor-edged arrow, struck down the head with its blazing earrings, its turban, and its helm.

sanskrit: tac chiraḥ prāpatad bhūmau śyenāhṛtam ivāmiṣam tato 'sya kāyo vasudhāṃ paścāt prāpa tadā cyutaḥ
english: That head fell upon the ground like a piece of flesh borne off by a hawk; then his body, falling thereafter, reached the earth.

sanskrit: tasmin hate mahārāja trastās tasya padānugāḥ gautamaṃ samare tyaktvā dudruvus te diśo daśa
english: When he was slain, O great king, his followers, struck with terror, abandoned the son of Gautama in the fight and fled to the ten quarters.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ tu samare saṃnivārya mahābalaḥ kṛtavarmābravīd dhṛṣṭas tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti pārṣatam
english: But the mighty Kṛtavarman, having checked Dhṛṣṭadyumna in the fight, said boldly to the son of Pṛṣata, "Stand, stand!"

sanskrit: tad abhūt tumulaṃ yuddhaṃ vṛṣṇipārṣatayo raṇe āmiṣārthe yathā yuddhaṃ śyenayor gṛddhayor nṛpa
english: Then there was a tumultuous battle between the Vṛṣṇi and the son of Pṛṣata in the field, like the strife of two hawks greedy for a morsel of flesh, O king.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu samare hārdikyaṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ ājaghānorasi kruddhaḥ pīḍayan hṛdikātmajam
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna in the fight struck Hārdikya in the chest with nine arrows, in his wrath sorely afflicting the son of Hṛdika.

sanskrit: kṛtavarmā tu samare pārṣatena dṛḍhāhataḥ pārṣataṃ sarathaṃ sāśvaṃ chādayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: But Kṛtavarman, struck hard by the son of Pṛṣata in the fight, covered the son of Pṛṣata, chariot and horses, with his shafts.

sanskrit: sarathaś chādito rājan dhṛṣṭadyumno na dṛśyate meghair iva paricchanno bhāskaro jaladāgame
english: Covered over with his chariot, O king, Dhṛṣṭadyumna could not be seen, like the sun veiled by clouds at the coming of the rains.

sanskrit: vidhūya taṃ bāṇagaṇaṃ śaraiḥ kanakabhūṣaṇaiḥ vyarocata raṇe rājan dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ kṛtavraṇaḥ
english: Shaking off that mass of arrows with his own gold-adorned shafts, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, though wounded, shone forth in battle, O king.

sanskrit: tatas tu pārṣataḥ kruddhaḥ śastravṛṣṭiṃ sudāruṇām kṛtavarmāṇam āsādya vyasṛjat pṛtanāpatiḥ
english: Then the son of Pṛṣata, enraged, that commander of the host, closing upon Kṛtavarman, let loose a most terrible shower of weapons.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā śastravṛṣṭiṃ nirantarām śarair anekasāhasrair hārdikyo vyadhamad yudhi
english: That unbroken downpour of weapons rushing suddenly upon him Hārdikya scattered in the fight with many thousands of arrows.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu dāritāṃ yuddhe śastravṛṣṭiṃ duruttarām kṛtavarmāṇam abhyetya vārayām āsa pārṣataḥ
english: Seeing his hard-to-withstand shower of weapons rent asunder in the fight, the son of Pṛṣata closed upon Kṛtavarman and held him in check.

sanskrit: sārathiṃ cāsya tarasā prāhiṇod yamasādanam bhallena śitadhāreṇa sa hataḥ prāpatad rathāt
english: And swiftly he sent his charioteer to the abode of Yama with a sharp-edged broad arrow; slain, the man fell from the chariot.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnas tu balavāñ jitvā śatruṃ mahāratham kauravān samare tūrṇaṃ vārayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: Then the mighty Dhṛṣṭadyumna, having vanquished that great car-warrior, his foe, at once held back the Kauravas in the fight with his shafts.

sanskrit: tatas te tāvakā yodhā dhṛṣṭadyumnam upādravan siṃhanādaravaṃ kṛtvā tato yuddham avartata
english: Thereupon your warriors rushed against Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and raising a lion's roar, the battle then went on.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca drauṇir yudhiṣṭhiraṃ dṛṣṭvā śaineyenābhirakṣitam draupadeyais tathā śūrair abhyavartata hṛṣṭavat
english: Saṃjaya said: Droṇa's son, seeing Yudhiṣṭhira guarded by the grandson of Śini and by the valiant sons of Draupadī, advanced upon him as though in joy.

sanskrit: kirann iṣugaṇān ghorān svarṇapuṅkhāñ śilāśitān darśayan vividhān mārgāñ śikṣārthaṃ laghuhastavat
english: Scattering dread volleys of arrows, gold-nocked and whetted on stone, displaying his manifold passes of skill with a deft and nimble hand,

sanskrit: tataḥ khaṃ pūrayām āsa śarair divyāstramantritaiḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ ca samare paryavārayad astravit
english: he then filled the sky with arrows charged by celestial-weapon mantras, and that master of arms hemmed in Yudhiṣṭhira in the fight.

sanskrit: drauṇāyaniśaracchannaṃ na prājñāyata kiṃ cana bāṇabhūtam abhūt sarvam āyodhanaśiro hi tat
english: Veiled by the arrows of Drauṇāyani, nothing whatever could be discerned; that whole front of the battlefield had become one mass of arrows.
